children: BTCUSD fell as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $1.245 billion in outflows from Nov. 16–20, marking a third straight week above $1 billion. November withdrawals reached about $3.47 billion.
BTCUSD traded near $60,000, below JPMorgan’s estimated $86,000 average bitcoin mining cost. MARA sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion, using proceeds to repay loans and fund its AI shift.
Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows rose over the past two weeks, topping the prior four-week period. JPMorgan said retail investors drove most exits, while Bitcoin CME futures positioning fell modestly.
Abraxas Capital appears to have bought 10,356 Bitcoin vs US Dollar, Spot CFD (BTCUSD) on November 21 at an average price of about $58,651 per coin, for a reported total of approximately $607 million.
About 112,000 Bitcoin options were set to expire Friday at 08:00 UTC. Nearly 75% of puts were in the money, while Deribit’s $73,000 max-pain price sat above BTCUSD’s market price.
BTCUSD traders watched support near $55,000. Peter Brandt said past major bull markets ended with drops of at least 75%; applying that to the latest peak implies about $37,600.
On Nov. 20, Robert Kiyosaki said he welcomed BTCUSD’s decline and will buy more after a new low and signs of a bottom. He cited Bitcoin’s 21 million coin cap and prior buying at $20,000.
BTCUSD fell during the Strait of Hormuz crisis, alongside gold. OMFIF said Bitcoin’s dependence on online infrastructure and cyberattack risks limit its potential as a central-bank reserve asset.
The Czech National Bank established a $1 million test portfolio in November last year that includes Bitcoin alongside U.S. dollar stablecoins and tokenized deposits.
21Shares forecasts BTCUSD will hit a new all-time high in 2027, but says the market cycle may peak later, potentially after the 2028 halving.
